steps.text: This alert about lsass.exe writing a registry value with "\RunTime\" in the path looks like it could be a false positive, likely just matching the "\Run" substring rather than an actual persistence mechanism. I should check the actual registry path relation to confirm.

arguments.reasoning: Read the registry write details (key path, value, process) for the trigger relation.
Check the registry key path to see whether it is an autostart Run key or a benign RunTime path.
Verify lsass.exe image path, parent and signature legitimacy.

steps.text: This registry value is just Windows Secure Time Seeding activity from lsass, a normal routine process — I'll mark it benign.

submission.reasoning: False positive. The '\Run' rule matched on the substring '\RunTime\'. The value lsass.exe wrote is HKLM\System\CurrentControlSet\Services\W32Time\SecureTimeLimits\RunTime\SecureTimeTickCount. Windows Secure Time Seeding (W32Time) uses this key to store a QWORD tick count, and it updates it routinely. It is not an autostart Run key. The process is the genuine C:\windows\system32\lsass.exe on workstation5. The data written is a plain QWORD counter (0x37ec4871), not a command or file path, so this is not persistence.
